description: Three rows show sign and magnitude, ones' complement, and two's complement for +0, +5, −0, and −28. Each entry is an 8-bit binary number in groups of four bits. Two-way arrows link sign and magnitude to ones' complement, then ones' complement to two's complement. The text on the right gives the forward conversion rules for negative numbers.

frames.explanation: The highest bit is the sign bit. For +0 and +5, all three representations agree. For a negative number, keep the high bit 1 and invert the low seven bits to get ones' complement. Add 1 and keep the low eight bits to get two's complement. The table applies this rule to −28. To go back, subtract 1 from the two's complement value, then keep the sign bit and invert the low seven bits to recover sign and magnitude. For −0, adding 1 to its ones' complement, 1111 1111, gives the nine-bit result 1 0000 0000. Discarding the carry leaves 0000 0000, the same as +0, so the original positive and negative zeros can no longer be distinguished.
frames.title: Eight-bit sign and magnitude, ones' complement, and two's complement

summary: Compare the conversions for positive and negative numbers to see why two's complement has only one representation of zero.
